pointers.sentence: `django/utils/module_loading.py` is how Django reaches code it knows only by name: `import_string` turns a dotted path written as text into the class, function or module it names, `module_has_submodule` asks whether a package has a submodule without running it, and `autodiscover_modules` imports a module of one name from every installed application.

The code that reads the setting imports the path: `BaseHandler.load_middleware` for each middleware ([Building the middleware chain](../handlers/chain.md)), `get_hashers` for the password hashers (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.load_middleware`, `django/contrib/auth/hashers.py:get_hashers`).

The code that reads the setting imports the path: `BaseHandler.load_middleware` for each middleware ([Building the middleware chain](../handlers/chain.md)), `get_hashers` for the password hashers (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.load_middleware`, `django/contrib/auth/hashers.py:get_hashers`).
`import_string` takes a path and returns what it names (`django/utils/module_loading.py:import_string`).

`import_string` accepts a module's path, a top-level one included, where a top-level module failed and a submodule worked only if already imported; and it favours a submodule over a same-named attribute of its package, where the answer used to depend on what had been imported before (`docs/releases/6.2.txt`).

Each import in `import_string` goes through `cached_import`, which returns the module in `sys.modules` if it is there with a spec not marked as still initializing, and otherwise calls `importlib.import_module` (`django/utils/module_loading.py:cached_import`).
`module_has_submodule` says whether a package has a submodule of a given name, without running it (`django/utils/module_loading.py:module_has_submodule`).

`AppConfig.create` asks it whether an application has an apps submodule to look in for its configuration class and `AppConfig.import_models` whether it has a models submodule ([Populating the app registry](../startup/populate.md)), and the migrate command whether it has a management module (`django/apps/config.py:AppConfig.create`, `django/apps/config.py:AppConfig.import_models`, `django/core/management/commands/migrate.py:Command.handle`).

`autodiscover_modules` imports each module name it is given from every installed application, in the order of `INSTALLED_APPS` (`django/utils/module_loading.py:autodiscover_modules`).

Its user in Django is the admin: `django.contrib.admin.autodiscover` calls it for `"admin"` with the default site as the registry, and `AdminConfig.ready` calls that as Django starts ([Registering models: `AdminSite.register` and `ModelAdmin`](../admin/registration.md)) (`django/contrib/admin/__init__.py:autodiscover`).
`qualname` goes the other way: it returns a module's name, or a class's or a function's `__module__` and `__qualname__` joined by a dot (`django/utils/module_loading.py:qualname`).

A task is pickled as its function's path ([Background tasks: `Task`, `TaskResult` and the task backends](../services/tasks.md)) (`django/tasks/base.py:Task.__reduce__`, `django/tasks/base.py:Task.module_path`), the migration serializer writes functions and classes by it ([Serializing values: `serializer_factory` and `deconstruct`](../migrations/serializer.md)), and a URL pattern names its view by it (`django/urls/resolvers.py:URLPattern.lookup_str`).

`module_dir` returns a package's only entry of `__path__`, or else the directory of the module's file, and raises `ValueError` for a namespace package spread over several directories, which has neither (`django/utils/module_loading.py:module_dir`).
